text:
Maya: Heads-up from canary: warmup tasks hang on a handful of gzipped safetensors bundles. Pattern: repeated small-range 206s and post-decompress checksum mismatches. Not OOM, just no progress.
infra-bot: [alert] warmup_read_flap model=dialog-3 shard=shard-02
Jon: can you paste the trimmed logs?
Maya: sure:
```
2026-04-20T15:12:01Z loader fetch range 0-65535 -> 206
2026-04-20T15:12:01Z loader decompress -> invalid stream
2026-04-20T15:12:01Z verify post-decompress expected=1a2b3c got=000000
2026-04-20T15:12:02Z retry backoff=35ms
```
Sofia: sounds like a gzip header/CRC being split across ranges. We verify after decompress today which fails if the stream is truncated.
Jon: immediate options: (A) increase initial priming window (e.g., 128k) — easy but wastes bytes for small shards, (B) on checksum fail run a single "elastic prime" (e.g., 512k) then reverify, or (C) add compressed digest(s) to manifest and verify compressed bytes before decompressing.
Maya: I ran (B) in a micro-canary and it eliminated the stalls with negligible bandwidth impact.
Sofia: hybrid policy seems best: keep small priming by default; on first checksum fail trigger elastic prime; if manifest contains `compression.digest_sha256` then verify compressed bytes first and skip elastic prime.
Jon: propose manifest additions: `compression.type` (string), `compression.digest_sha256` (optional string), and optional sidecar `compression.index` (array of chunk digests) for long-term. Loader rules: if digest present -> compressed-verify path; else -> elastic-prime fallback.
Maya: metrics we should add: `loader.gz_checksum_mismatch`, `loader.gz_elastic_primes`, `loader.gz_compressed_verify_fail`, each tagged by `model`, `shard`, `region`, `canary`.
Sofia: tests: unit for partial-gzip headers; integration using an HTTP stub that returns split ranges; e2e canary with synthetic gzipped bundles. Also run CDN re-chunking sim to ensure chunking doesn't break compressed digest assumptions.
Jon: retry/backoff policy: exponential backoff with jitter, max 3 retries for range reads. On repeated checksum mismatch escalate to elastic prime; only after elastic prime fails do we fetch full compressed blob for a final verify.
Maya: note storage guidance: prefer publishing uncompressed safetensors for hot shards. If compression used, publish `compression.digest_sha256` and optionally `compression.index` (generated by publisher tooling). We should document CDN compatibility caveats.
Sofia: long-term RFC idea: per-compressed-chunk index (sidecar) so loader can validate small ranges without elastic priming. That requires publisher changes and backward-compat handling.
Jon: ownership: Sofia -> manifest schema + publisher example and docs; Maya -> small canary to roll elastic-prime change; I'll own loader changes and tests.
Maya: I'll open INF-9922 summarizing the plan and attach a rollout checklist and dashboards.
infra-bot: ticket INF-9922 created: "gzipped safetensors: elastic-prime + compressed-verify + sidecar index" assigned eng-ml.
Maya: thanks all. If canary shows any regressions I'll call for rollback. :+1:
